rationale_evidence.statement: Maps the Zero lens's five questions onto the Ashtavakra Gita's own claims: what is represented (universe, body, mind, knowledge, experience), what is assumed away (the universe's independence from consciousness), what is absent (independent reality of the universe, i.e. mithya), what is undefined (the true nature of the Self until realized), and what is unrepresented (Brahman/consciousness itself, which the text holds cannot be represented at all).

rationale_evidence.anchor: The universe, being unreal, appears like a snake in a rope. ... What is represented (the universe) is not independently real. ... All phenomena arise in your consciousness, they are experienced in your consciousness and disappear in your consciousness. Knowledge is not a thing to be stored -- it is an appearance. ... the knower is not represented in the knowledge state -- it is the witness. ... All other knowledge is mithya (false). Only self-knowledge is real.
rationale_evidence.statement: Draws four textual insights from the Gita: representation is never independently real (the universe, though represented, borrows its reality, 'like a snake in a rope'); knowledge is not a thing to be stored but an appearance arising, experienced, and disappearing in consciousness; the knower is not represented in the knowledge state -- it is the witness, unattached to body/mind; and self-knowledge (Tat tvam asi) is the only real knowledge, all other knowledge being mithya.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Is KnowledgeOS modeling reality or appearance? If reality: Ashtavakra says there is no reality other than consciousness. If appearance: Ashtavakra says all appearances are mithya (false). ... KnowledgeOS assumes there is a state to be known. Ashtavakra says there is only consciousness. ... This is a fundamental challenge to the entire KnowledgeOS enterprise.
rationale_evidence.statement: Poses the text's central challenge to KnowledgeOS as a dilemma: is KnowledgeOS modeling reality or appearance -- if reality, Ashtavakra holds there is no reality other than consciousness; if appearance, all appearances are mithya (false). KnowledgeOS assumes there is a state to be known; Ashtavakra says there is only consciousness -- framed as a fundamental challenge to the entire KnowledgeOS enterprise, closing with the unresolved 'Mithya question for the Kernel': how should KnowledgeOS model the relationship between representation and reality.

rationale_evidence.statement: A formal DDD critical review names the core methodological error in the prior Constitutional Kernel proposal: an architectural metaphor (constitutional adjudicator) was treated as a domain concept and then used as a container for every responsibility that seemed important, producing a 'god object.'

rationale_evidence.statement: Separating adjudication from execution too aggressively risks a transactional gap: the aggregate's state could change between the moment admissibility is determined and the moment the transition is actually applied, so who owns the actual state mutation (Kernel vs Application/Workflow) needs a stronger transactional answer than a simple 'Kernel says ADMISSIBLE, then Application executes' handoff.
